message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Atlantic Avenue.

I have $463 and own a green monopoly. Atlantic is the remaining yellow property in the auction. The current bid is $14. I previously considered mortgaging it for $130.

p3 has $91 and p4 has $74. I will bid at least $75 to clear p4, or $92 to clear p3. I will not exceed $130. Winning under that cap gives me a profit from the mortgage arbitrage and denies the other players cash.

I will bid $15 to clear p4. If p3 wins, they would profit $39-$115 from the mortgage arbitrage, which is dangerous because they just mortgaged everything to pay rent and now need cash badly.

I must win this auction to block the cash infusion. If p3 buys for $50, they would have $41 left and mortgage for $130, ending with $171. That would let them survive and hotel their pinks. If p4 wins cheap, they would mortgage for $130 and use that cash to build more on Park Place and Boardwalk. I will bid $92 to clear p3 and secure the property.

I am weighing whether to jump straight to $92 or min-raise. Both players will match every dollar anyway, so the end result is the same. I already own Ventnor, giving me two of three yellows.

Jumping to $92 nets $501 total cash after mortgaging, a gain of $38 over my current balance. I am weighing whether to bid $15 and wait, or commit the full $92 now. p3's earlier bids suggest they may be testing rather than fully committed to their $91 cap. p4 seems more likely to reach his $74 limit. The risk is paying $92 if either player bluffs and drops out early.

Rational bidding will push the price to $92. If I drop out and p3 wins at $15, they gain roughly $115 in cash and could survive or hotel their pinks. I will bid $92 to secure the property and block that cash infusion.

I will post "$92" as my public bid. A rational player with $91 and positive expected value will not drop out at $75, so min-raising through multiple turns is unnecessary.
